questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}8y=6 \\ -5x=7-6y\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}8y=6 \\ -5x+6y=7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}]$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot 0-(-5)\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+6y=46 \\ 8x+y=-23\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 8 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}46 \\ -23\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 8 & 1\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 1-6\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -8 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{46}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -8 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{46}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -8 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}46 \\ -23\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x=y+1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=1 \\ x-y=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot (-1)-5\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
